one_liner: Serve as a Contracting Officer's Representative helping the federal courts' IT office buy and manage software licenses, hardware, cloud and IT services contracts.
fit_summary: The posting requires a full year of experience in ALL three areas: managing federal IT contracts, justifying resource requirements for complex programs, and accounting/finance analytical skills. Daniel's IEM consulting background may touch government contracts, but nothing on file shows federal IT contract management or COR work. Daniel's policy knowledge and people skills are real strengths but are not what this job screens for.
eligibility: Open to the public (hiring paths include public, fed-competitive, fed-excepted, vet), so Daniel can apply without federal status.

Specialized experience: at least 52 weeks covering ALL of managing federal IT contracts, resource requirement formulation/justification for complex programs, and accounting/finance with analytical software tools.
No education requirement and no security clearance, but you must pass an FBI fingerprint check and a public trust suitability check.
Mandatory narrative responses are required; missing them means no full rating credit.
The salary range is wide ($102,415-$191,965, AD-00 pay band) and suggests a senior-level role; a trial period applies to first-time federal hires.
strategy: Before applying, honestly check whether your IEM work included federal contract tasks such as task order support, deliverable tracking, invoicing, cost estimates, or proposal pricing. If you can't document a year of all three specialized areas, treat this as a stretch application.

Frame IEM experience in contract language: name the federal client and contract type if allowed, describe your role on [contract/task order], and use terms like statements of work, deliverables, burn rate, and invoices where they are accurate.

Fit it on two pages: for each IEM role list dates, hours per week, and 3-5 bullets that map directly to the three specialized experience areas, citing the analytical tools you used (e.g., [Excel/Power BI]).

Answer the questionnaire and mandatory narratives truthfully, because self-ratings are checked against your resume and downgraded if unsupported. Back every 'expert' answer with a matching resume bullet.
Apply well before the November 3, 2026 close (it opens October 20). Consider earning FAC-COR Level I/II training, available via FAI, to strengthen future acquisition applications.
In parallel, target better-fit roles such as FEMA program/external affairs, Virginia VDEM, local emergency management, or legislative staff positions that use your policy and relationship strengths.
resume_bullets: Supported [federal client] emergency management contract by tracking [number] deliverables against the statement of work and flagging schedule or quality issues to [project manager/client COR].
Developed cost estimates and staffing/resource justifications for [program/proposal] worth [$ amount] using [Excel/analytical tool], coordinating with finance and technical leads.
Reviewed [number] contractor invoices and monthly status reports for accuracy against contract terms on [contract name], resolving discrepancies with [stakeholders].
interview_questions: Describe your experience serving as or supporting a COR on a federal IT contract. What did you monitor and how?
How would you build an independent government cost estimate for an enterprise software license renewal?
Tell us about a time a contractor underperformed. How did you document it and advise the contracting officer?
How do you conduct market research to recommend a contract vehicle or procurement method?
watch_outs: The specialized experience bar (federal IT contract management plus finance skills) likely exceeds what is on file for Daniel, so you may be rated not qualified.
The heavy focus on software license agreements and IT acquisitions is technical and has little overlap with policy or public-facing work.
The job is in DC with telework but is not remote, so plan for a commute from Manassas (VRE is an option).
The application window is only two weeks (Oct 20 to Nov 3, 2026), and the narratives are mandatory.
